A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabSTAR research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–G support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and regression benchmark results, architectural experiments, and ablations in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds baseline evaluations, computational cost measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The five-stage architecture, target-aware tokens, numerical encoding, interaction transformer, objectives, and pretraining/LoRA procedure remain unchanged. Clarifications about independent feature fusion and which layers receive LoRA adapters document the existing method rather than establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both retain the reported 350-dataset pretraining corpus, 50-dataset benchmark comprising 14 classification and 36 regression tasks, and 20-dataset ablation subset. The new feature-count cost study samples existing pretraining datasets without establishing additional domain or prediction-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated LightGBM, RealMLP, TabM, TabICL, and TabDPT baselines, including tuned and unlimited variants where applicable. Appendix G newly compares existing ablation variants against external baselines. Cost comparisons also change membership, omitting previously timed TabPFN-v2 and CARTE and introducing a CPU-only CatBoost control.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands computational evaluation to separate training and inference latency and peak CPU/GPU memory, adds a CPU-only control, and evaluates feature-count groups across 45 sampled datasets. Appendix F.4 reports A100/8-core hardware for most evaluations, replacing v1's heterogeneous compute setup. Main prediction splits, sample limits, and four-hour tuning budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds qualitative tests of column names, target-value verbalization, and dataset-description prefixes. Appendix F.5 adds feature-count sensitivity measurements for runtime and memory. These extend the analysis while retaining the original encoder-unfreezing, pretraining-scale, and numerical-verbalization ablation results.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random train-test splits and 95% confidence intervals using the same normal approximation. Expanded result tables retain this practice. Newly reported hyperparameter-trial counts describe optimization effort, not additional statistical replication.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline and cost results and revises existing entries. For C09 at 10K, TabSTAR AUROC changes from 99.3±0.1 to 94.0±0.8 and CatBoost-Tuned from 99.8±0.1 to 82.6±1.4, reversing their ranking (v1 Table 17; v2 Table 19). These revisions are unexplained. Aggregate scores and win rates also change; normalized scores use different comparator pools and cannot establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal architecture definitions, numerical transformations, sequence construction, and mathematical objectives are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears; the added discussion of attention costs and class-token counts elaborates existing architecture properties.

C1.justification: The central claims about target-aware representations, classification leadership, and benefits from pretraining scale remain. The conclusion newly claims GBDT-level inference efficiency relative to ICL models and explicitly extends the future vision to tabular data combining numerical, textual, and image features.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes slower training from inexpensive inference and attributes much baseline inference cost to text embedding generation. It adds class-count-related memory limitations, interprets feature-width cost growth, and proposes distribution-aware numerical encoding for regression. Existing regression, few-shot, and numerical-only evaluation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds baseline implementation information and RealMLP/LightGBM hyperparameter search spaces. Appendix F adds hardware disclosures, feature-group profiling details, and per-dataset tuning-trial counts. Appendix B clarifies LoRA placement. These substantially expand experimental documentation, while the code-access disclosure remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SCARF, LightGBM, TabDPT, and a self-supervised tabular-learning survey. Related work explicitly limits its scope to supervised learning and expands discussion of TabICL and TabDPT. The broader positioning around semantic, target-aware tabular foundation models remains stable.

P1.justification: The title changes to emphasize tabular data with text fields. Local rewrites clarify architecture, benchmark construction, and finetuning terminology, while Appendix F gains more explicit subdivisions. Conference, acknowledgment, and funding text change, but the main section sequence and most narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 are redesigned to group default/tuned and 10K/unlimited variants. Figures 5–8 add scaling and ablation-comparison displays. New cost, hyperparameter, and trial-count tables accompany substantially widened result tables and transposed win-rate tables. The original pretraining-scale summary is retained as v2 Table 29 after relocation from the main text.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons address v1's important omission of strong MLP and additional foundation-model baselines, materially strengthening evaluation of its classification claim. More consistent hardware reporting and separate inference, training, and memory measurements substantially improve assessment of practical costs. These gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses, including unexplained C09 revisions and the conflict between excluding TabDPT regression results and reporting a regression win rate in Table 23.
